title: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report — US crude, gasoline and distillate stocks for the week ending 2026-09-25 (10:30 ET, quarter-end morning, the day before ISM Manufacturing)
source: EST: eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 52,322 bytes) and read from its own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher. It states verbatim that the summary and Tables 1-14 are released 'after 10:30 a.m. eastern time on Wednesday', and its Holiday Release Schedule names 2026 exceptions ONLY for the weeks ending 01-16, 02-13, 05-22, 09-04, 10-09 and 11-06. The week ending 2026-09-25 is not among them, so the standard rule applies unmodified; 2026-09-30 is a Wednesday and 2026-09-25 is the Friday five days before it. TWO REASONS THIS IS `estimate`, NEITHER OF THEM DATE DOUBT, AND THE FIRST IS WEAKER THAN ITS 09-16 SIBLING'S: (1) the date is DERIVED from the publisher's stated cadence plus weekday arithmetic, not read off a dated row — eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ (fetched direct 2026-09-15, HTTP 200, 72,333 bytes) currently names only 'Next Release Date: Sep. 16, 2026', and will not name 09-30 until the 09-23 release publishes; (2) market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines NO `EIA:` prefix (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:), the same schema gap eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16 and every eia-steo-* entry record — adding one would confirm this whole class and is a schema change, not this lane's call. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH, 2026-09-15 (D-15, the outermost `low` cadence band), after reading the one proposal that named this id — proposals/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-30.from-ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01.json, filed by the ISM lane the same day. That proposal's ATTRIBUTION rationale is adopted unchanged: this is the last weekly US inventory read published before ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01, whose live claim FT-ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01-1 (Prices >= 73.0) credits the Iran/Gulf supply shock. THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDS A SECOND REASON THE PROPOSAL DID NOT HAVE, and it is a measurement rather than a hunch: 2026-09-30 covers the week ending 09-25, three weeks past the 97.8% refinery utilization printed for the week ending 09-04 — squarely inside the fall turnaround season. Across 1993-2025 the WPSR week ending nearest Sep 25 printed utilization BELOW 96.0 in 32 of 33 years (sole exception 1997, 98.1), and every one of the three genuine high-base analogs (base >= 97.0: 1997, 1998, 2018) DECLINED, median -3.60 points. EIA's own September 2026 STEO states the mechanism verbatim: 'Distillate production typically decreases during the fall refinery maintenance season.' Two convergent point estimates — 97.8 plus the high-base median delta, and 2025's 91.4 target week plus 2026's +2.9 y/y spread — both land near 94.2-94.3. STOCKS, BY CONTRAST, ARE A COIN FLIP over the same three weeks (2016-2025: crude built in 4 of 10 years, distillate 4 of 10, gasoline 4 of 10), so NO stock-direction claim is made. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is tiered low deliberately: no house playbook is energy-keyed, no tracked symbol carries direct crude exposure, and `symbols` is EMPTY on purpose — populating it with XLE/USO would assert an exposure this lane does not hold. Context at writing (2026-09-15, ~16:13 ET): WTI 106.01, Brent 108.80, HO 5.0109/gal (a ~$2.49/gal crack), XLE 65.93, USO 161.86, VIX 17.28. Full ledger with sources: docs/research/events/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-30.md. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
